insight.title: The Star on Elevator Buttons Isn't a Decoration
insight.subtitle: It is a tactile escape route mandated by building codes to guide you out in a pitch-black emergency.
insight.notificationHook: Why elevator buttons have a star

sections.text: Next time you step into an elevator, look at the panel. Next to the "L" or "1" button, you’ll almost always see a raised star symbol. It isn’t a design aesthetic.
It is a safety feature designed for pitch-black emergencies. If a fire cuts the power and fills the building with smoke, that embossed star tells your fingers exactly which button leads outside.

By making the exit floor tactilely distinct, building codes ensure that anyone—whether visually impaired or trapped in a dark, panicked evacuation—can locate the safety of the street-level exit by touch alone.
It’s not a gold star for arriving; it’s a map for escaping.
